brief: Goldman's basics note frames four threads. Asia rallied overnight (Nikkei +3%, KOSPI +1.7%, Taiwan +0.8%) on Micron follow-through and quarter-end reversion, reinforcing an unchanged bullish AI view: inference demand (Muse, Dots, Autopilot, Grok) is accelerating, Google's Gemini 4/Argon launched with strong benchmarks but limited real-world evidence yet, and Oracle's reported $7bn Tencent chip deal adds to a physical-constraint thesis (firm H200/B200 rental pricing, scarce spot compute) that argues against being bearish compute makers. On Micron, cycle-peak worries are outrun by pricing and earnings momentum, with FY27 supply tight and 2027 HBM pricing above 2026, though the multiple reset already prices in cycle risk. Rates: the back end stays bidless despite a lighter PCE print; an October move looks less likely, but curve stress sits further out, with payrolls and ISM the next catalysts. France's 2027 budget targets a ~5.0% deficit via ~54bn euros of adjustment, but Goldman argues the opposition's response matters more than the plan itself, and flags a EUR downside tail if a future government targets France's EU contribution. Iran-US talks remain stalled but alive through Qatar.
